# AI Thinks this Post is Terrible (but I’m writing it anyway)


### Using Expected Parrot to propose and prioritize blogging topics


[John Horton](https://substack.com/@johnjhorton)


Sep 15, 2026


I took a break on blogging this summer to go heads-down on a bunch of new Expected Parrot features and research ideas. We have a


**lot** to talk about—so much that I was feeling a bit overwhelmed in what, exactly, to focus on. I needed some way to:


1.


Map all the new features to good blog post topics


2.


Rate those topics by likely reader interest


Naturally, I thought “maybe AI could help?” I used the following prompt with our conversational research agent (


[www.expectedparrot.com](http://www.expectedparrot.com/) ):


Thanks for reading! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.


The full report is


[here](https://www.expectedparrot.com/research-agent/share/rzMe4hfqb8d75tbFwxCg7Q) which has my transcript. As it’s designed to do, it asked me a bunch of clarifying questions:


The research agent also used


[Firecrawl](https://www.firecrawl.dev/) to do a bit more research about the company and what we’re doing. This research was then used in the creation of the AI Agent personas that evaluated the topics:


As I was working with it, I remembered that AI’s asked to rate things are way too nice and will claim to read everything, click everything, buy everything, etc. What I needed to do was do some forces comparisons so I asked it to try to ranking questions and then fit a


[Bradley-Terry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bradley%E2%80%93Terry_model) model. This was the end result: 25 blog topics rank-ordered by score. See the transcript for details and note that you are reading a last-from-the-bottom example:


Also note that dead last is a blog post idea I have on using AI for


[morphological analysis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morphological_analysis_(problem-solving)) which I thought would be a banger. I actually will still write that one—AI isn’t the boss of me—but I’m definitely also more inclined to write the top performers.


It’s not terribly important given the stakes of this post/decision, but I want to flag that you can see precisely how the end report was generating, starting from the code that generated the options and the code that generated the personas being used:


Now, you might say “John - how do you


*know* this is what people want?” The truth, is, I don’t and I could imagine the AI answers differ from what some high-quality market research would reveal. But the bigger truth is that I don’t have the money, time or inclination to do serious market research on this. The status quo was just to go with my gut. Instead, I can do this which is I think quite a bit better and more interesting for less money. Anyway, can’t wait to tell you more about Morphological Analysis!


PS - the agents


*really* didn’t like the Morphological analysis idea


Thanks for reading! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.
